newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Mozart opera recreated in cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Mozart opera recreated in cyberspace.

text.p: Austria's 18th century composer Mozart is launched into cyberspace in a new avant-garde production of one his most popular operas at the Salzburg annual summer festival.
The digitalised version of "The Abduction from the Seraglio", which opens on Wednesday evening, pushes the boundaries of the festival's traditionally conservative image.
On a stage littered with television and computer monitors, the real world meets the virtual as singers serenade projected images.
Behind the digital hype lies a concept that sets one of Mozart's most frequently performed works in cyberspace and questions where the digital highway is leading us.
In the original opera, three friends are abducted by pirates and held prisoner in a Turkish palace -- an exotic scenario much en vogue in late 18th century Europe.
Transposed into the digital age, the trio mysteriously disappear while surfing the Internet.
An e-mail gives a hint as to their whereabouts.
They have been captured in a powerful digital mesh, which threatens to transform them into computer data, wiping out their human existence.
The hero, Belmonte, sets out to rescue his beloved Konstanze and her entourage from their virtual abductor.

Musically, the opera has been recreated by young Austrian composer Peter Valentin. Every note of the score was digitally modulated or electronically produced based on analogue tones ranging from classical instruments to noise.
Valentin has developed an innovative sound language, which he calls a "contemporary instrumentation of Mozart's original music".
However, the producers are anxious to stress that this is not a superficial experiment with Mozart's genius.
When asked how much of Mozart's original score has had to suffer, director Hubert Lepka was quick to answer: "Not at all. It is our conventional way of listening to Mozart that is challenged."
The project has the support of Gerard Mortier, the director of the Salzburg Festival, which opened last weekend.
A classical version of the opera with the German title "Die Entfuehrung aus dem Serail" will also be staged as part of the festival's traditional programme.
